previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, diastolic heart failure, and depression was admitted for recurrent chest pain and dizziness. Initial evaluation revealed transient chest pain with non-specific EKG changes, but serial troponins were negative and prior stress test was normal, ruling out acute cardiac cause. Dizziness was attributed to orthostatic hypotension, likely exacerbated by dehydration and medication effects. Her creatinine was elevated on admission but normalized with IV hydration. Depression was identified as a contributing factor to her symptoms, and social work was consulted for counseling support. Medications were adjusted, including temporary hold of antihypertensives and reduction of spironolactone. She improved clinically, remained asymptomatic, and was discharged home with follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mrs ___ is a ___ yo F with DMII, gatroparesis, recent abx 
course for poorly defined small bowel process who presented with 
mild RLQ pain/tenderness and no other GI or systemic sxs.

# RLQ pain/tenderness: On admission, there was no concern for 
acute abdomen given the pts relatively benign exam.  Initially, 
we were concerned for continued inflammatory process given 
evidence of inflammation on prior CT, however repeat CT showed 
no evidence of inflammation.  Given that we had low suspicion 
for infection, abx were held.  The case was discussed with her 
primary gastroenerologist, Dr ___, as well as the GI consult 
team.  A colonoscopy was performed and was unremarkable, however 
the terminal ileum was poorly visualized do to inadequate prep.  
She was treated with supportive care including IVF, 
metoclopromide, pain control, anti-emetics and a bowel regimen 
for functional abd pain.  Her diet was advanced successfully on 
day 3 of her hospitalization and on discharge she was tolerating 
a full diet and was with only minimal pain.  She is scheduled to 
f/u with Dr ___ on discharge.

# Acute on chronic renal failure: This was felt to be due to 
poor PO intake in the setting of abd pain.  Her renal failure 
resolved with fluid repletion.
.

BRBPR and had a small crit drop which stabilized and improved 
the following day without transfusion.   She had no further 
episodes of bleeding.   Given that the rectum was poorly 
visualized on colonoscopy and there was no identifiable sources 
of bleeding, her BRBPR was attributed to bleeding internal 
hemorrhoids.

initiated.  Blood sugars were well controlled.

Bowel gas pattern is non-obstructive with air seen in non-dilated loops of

INDICATION:  ___ woman with history of nonspecific small bowel
inflammation, who now presents with recurrent abdominal pain.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images from the base of the lungs to the pubic
symphysis were obtained with the administration of IV contrast.  Multiplanar
reformatted images (axial, coronal, sagittal) were generated and reviewed.

FINDINGS:

CT ABDOMEN:  The visualized lung bases show no consolidation or pleural
effusion.  The visualized heart and pericardium are unremarkable.

The liver is homogenous in density with no focal lesions.  The patient is
status post cholecystectomy with surgical clips in the gallbladder fossa.  The
pancreas, spleen, adrenal glands are unremarkable.  The kidneys enhance and
excrete contrast symmetrically without hydronephrosis or stones.  A 25 x 26 mm
hypodense lesion within the right interpolar region is consistent with a
simple renal cyst, unchanged in size and appearance compared to ___.  Visualized intraabdominal loops of small and large bowel show no
obstruction, mass or bowel wall thickening.  There is no free air or free
fluid in the abdomen.  The mesenteric and retroperitoneal lymph nodes do not
meet size criteria for pathologic enlargement.  The intra-abdominal
vasculature is unremarkable.

CT OF THE PELVIS:  The pelvic loops of large and small bowel are unremarkable.
The bladder, distal ureters, rectum, and sigmoid colon are unremarkable. 
Pelvic lymph nodes do not meet CT criteria for lymphadenopathy.  The patient
is status post hysterectomy and bilateral oophorectomy.  An ovoid calcified
structure in the mid pelvis is unchanged in size and appearance since ___ and possibly represents a calcified hematoma or duplication cyst. 
There is no free pelvic fluid.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There are no lytic or sclerotic lesions worrisome for
malignancy.

1. Stable right interpolar region renal cyst.

appearance since ___ and possibly represents a calcified
